text:
Predicates:
Roses(x) ::: x are roses.
GivenOutOnTV(x) ::: x are given out on TV.
OnMondayAt8pm(x) ::: x are given out on TV on some Mondays at 8 pm.
Bachelor(x) ::: x are on the Bachelor.
PortraysLives(x) ::: x portrays the lives of real people.
RealityTV(x) ::: x are reality TV shows.
BreakingBad ::: the show Breaking Bad.
Premises:
∀x (Roses(x) ∧ GivenOutOnTV(x) ∧ OnMondayAt8pm(x)) ::: On some Mondays at 8 pm, roses are given out on TV.
∀x (GivenOutOnTV(x) → Bachelor(x)) ::: Every rose given out on TV is on the Bachelor.
∀x (Bachelor(x) → PortraysLives(x)) ::: Everything on the Bachelor portrays the lives of real people.
∀x (PortraysLives(x) → RealityTV(x)) ::: All shows portraying the lives of real people are reality TV shows.
¬RealityTV(BreakingBad) ::: Breaking Bad is not a reality TV show.
Conclusion:
∃x (GivenOutOnTV(x) ∧ Roses(x) ∧ OnMondayAt8pm(x)) ::: Roses are given out on TV on some Mondays at 8 pm.
∃x (GivenOutOnTV(x) ∧ Roses(x) ∧ OnMondayAt8pm(x) ∧ BreakingBad(x)) ::: Roses are given out on TV on some Mondays at 8 pm in Breaking Bad.
